mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% compresses discount rates in equity valuation models, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to reduced cost of capital for corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 2.5% correlates with negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases or rank correlation with returns is negative and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in 3 months correlates with positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases or rank correlation with returns is positive and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent 6-month GDP growth (GDPC1) above 0.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 0.3% confirm robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings expectations and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0.5% and INDPRO growth > 0.3% in 6 months
failure_condition: Joint GDPC1/INDPRO growth threshold exceeded but 20-day returns negative in >60% of cases or joint signal rank correlation with returns is negative and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL annual inflation > 2.5%) reduce liquidity and increase risk aversion, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher real interest rates.
failure_condition: Tightening cycle periods correlate with positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases or rank correlation between cycle condition and returns is positive and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) above 2,200 thousand units signals strong consumer demand and economic activity, increasing corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: HOUST above 2,200 thousand correlates with negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases or rank correlation with returns is negative and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% in 3 months signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months correlates with negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases or rank correlation with returns is negative and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month retail sales (RSAFS) growth above 0.3% and industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 0.2% confirm strong consumer and business demand, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.3% and INDPRO growth > 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: Joint RSAFS/INDPRO growth threshold exceeded but 20-day returns negative in >60% of cases or joint signal rank correlation with returns is negative and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% and UNRATE < 4.5% for 6 months) signal economic peak conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to overvaluation and anticipated monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 3.0% and UNRATE < 4.5% in 6 months
failure_condition: Late-cycle regime periods correlate with positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases or rank correlation between regime condition and returns is positive and significant (p < 0.05).
